subject: Model rollout p99 regression — urgent bridge & customer note
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Model rollout p99 regression — immediate bridge requested

Team,

We started seeing a clear p99 latency regression at 09:07 PST correlated with a staged rollout of the v2-int8-rc1 variant of redwood-13B on the gen-api-us route. Quick numbers:
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 before rollout: 140ms / 380ms / 620ms
- After rollout (09:07 — 09:10): 150ms / 560ms / 1620ms
- Observed throughput drop on gen-api-us: ~18% (spike in queueing + dropped prewarm hits)

Initial signals point to a runtime kernel divergence on sequence-length > 1024 requests (kernel fallback causes a CPU path for a subset of layers in the quantized variant). I've attached a short tail of service logs and the impact summary.

Immediate asks:
1) Can infra/SRE schedule a rollback for the variant to restore the previous stable model?
2) If rollback is risky, can we throttle rollout weight to 0% and pin QuickCart to previous model until we have a fix?
3) Product — prioritize a short postmortem (root cause or perf delta across sequence lengths) and confirm whether we can revert the shipping config (kernel selection flag).
4) CS — prepare a short customer note for QuickCart describing mitigation steps + ETA (aim for <1h).

I'm standing up a brief bridge (Zoom link in RUN-7892) to coordinate. I'll stay on the thread.

-karthik
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model rollout p99 regression — immediate bridge requested

Thanks Karthik — good catch. Quick plan from product/ops side:

1) Ben: please execute an immediate rollback of v2-int8-rc1 to the prior stable variant for gen-api-us. If rollback takes > 10m, implement a routing policy to force QuickCart requests to the stable shard only.
2) Marissa: we need a concise risk note on the trade-offs of disabling int8 fallback for long sequences vs. keeping the feature on. Ship a 3-bullet decision and postmortem template to RUN-7892.
3) Grace: please send the short customer note below (I drafted it) to Sasha/support with the rollback ETA and recommended temporary throttle (if they want to reduce p99 exposure).
4) Vivek: flag any billing/contract impacts if we maintain a hot-standby (dedicated capacity) while we remediate — CS may ask.

Draft customer note (please edit to tone + final recipient):
-----
Hi Sasha —
We detected a latency regression affecting some gen calls after a model variant rollout this morning. We are rolling back the change and expect improved latency within ~15 minutes of rollback completion. Whilst we remediate, you can temporarily reduce concurrency to reduce p99 exposure; our team will monitor and update you by EOD PST. Sorry for the disruption — we’re treating this as high priority.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
-----

I'll join the bridge now. If rollback is complete, reply with timestamps and attach post-rollback metrics.

- Laura

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model rollout p99 regression — immediate bridge requested

Rolling back now. Commands executed:
- rollback service:redwood-gen-api-us --variant=stable-20261130 --confirm
- flush-kv-cache --shard=gen-api-us --grace=30s

Rollback completed at 09:45 PST. Initial metrics (09:46 — 09:53): p50/p95/p99 = 145ms / 400ms / 630ms. Throughput back within 95% of baseline.

Notes:
- We saw a persistent low warm-hit ratio for the KV cache for sequences >1024 during the rollout; the quantized variant seems to miss cache prewarming paths, which explains the CPU path fallback.
- Short-term mitigation options: (A) prefill KV for high QPS customers (costly), (B) keep quant variant gated behind a rollout flag until we fix kernel path (preferred), (C) increase autoscaler headroom to hide per-request jitter (temporary).

Attaching logs and an impact summary. I'll open a follow-up ticket for a warmstart automation.

-ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
